title: Redwood Optimize v4 - Product PRD, Design, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Mariana Lopez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document describes Redwood Optimize v4 (ROptimize v4): the next major release of our cost-and-performance optimization toolkit for model serving. It consolidates product requirements (PRD), design specifications, roadmap and themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and the initial release notes and rollout plan. Intended audience: product, engineering, eng-platform, sales, and customer success.

Problem statement
- Customers running large-scale inference want to reduce per-token costs while preserving latency and quality.
- Existing v3 features (auto-batching, quantization suggestions, model recommendations) reduce costs but require manual tuning and lack workload-specific guidance.
- Teams need guardrails that connect cost controls to quality metrics and a low-friction upgrade path from hosted to dedicated/private deployments.

Goals (Product-level)
1) Reduce average per-token inference cost for eligible workloads by 20% (measured across pilot customers) without exceeding latency SLO degradation of 5%.
2) Provide workload-aware, one-click optimization suggestions and automated experiments (A/B) for batching, cache profiles, and quantization.
3) Surface quality/regression risk via integrated evals and prompt-set checks before applying optimizations.
4) Enable tiered packaging and usage incentives to convert free-tier experimentation into Dedicated/Private commitments.

Success metrics
- Cost: mean per-token billed cost reduction for pilot cohort >= 20% within 90 days of adoption.
- Latency: P95 latency increase <= 5% for 95% of requests after optimization.
- Quality: Regression rate (evals failing acceptance criteria) <= 2% for automated changes; manual review flow for remaining cases.
- Adoption: 10 enterprise customers on Optimize-paid tier within 6 months.

User stories & requirements
(Implementation requirements are in the table below.)
- As an ML engineer, I want one-click apply of suggested optimization bundles with automatic rollback on quality regressions.
- As a platform engineer, I want to preview resource and cost impact of an optimization before applying it to production.
- As a product manager, I want a new pricing tier that aligns incentives for reserved capacity purchases.

Requirements (summary table)
- ID | Requirement | Priority | Owner | Acceptance criteria
- R-001 | Workload profiling engine: collect length distribution, cold-start rates, and KV-cache hit rates per route | Must | eng-serving-runtime | Profiles available in console and API; sample size >=100k tokens/day per route
- R-002 | Suggestion engine: generate parameterized optimization bundles (batch size, pad-to, quantization profile, cache TTL) with cost/latency/quality delta estimates | Must | product + eng-serving-runtime | Suggestions include estimated delta (cost %, latency %), confidence score, and rationale
- R-003 | Automated experiment runner: ability to run canary/A-B tests with automatic statistical evaluation and rollback policies | Must | eng-platform | Experiment results show cost/latency/quality delta; automatic rollback if regression detected
- R-004 | Eval integration: attach pre-defined prompt sets and accuracy metrics to validation pipeline; run before/after comparison | Must | applied-ml-and-evals | Regression risk flagged; results stored for audit
- R-005 | One-click apply and rollback UI + API + audit logs | Must | eng-developer-experience | Apply completes within expected time; rollback within SLA; audit entry with actor and diff
- R-006 | Pricing/packaging: new Optimize Pro tier tied to reserved capacity discounts and feature gating | Should | finance-and-legal + product | Pricing table defined; discount logic implemented; billing test cases pass
- R-007 | Access controls and confidentiality: ensure customer keys and audit trails are not exposed during optimize workflow | Must | security-and-compliance | Pass security review and automated scans

Design spec (high level)
- Components:
  - Profiler service (read-only) that consumes request telemetry and emits daily workload profiles per route/model.
  - Suggestion engine that takes profiles + historical experiment outcomes and returns ranked bundles with estimated deltas.
  - Experiment runner orchestrator that configures routing rules, applies optimization to a percentage of traffic, and collects metrics.
  - Eval hook integration that runs predefined prompt sets on candidate model/config variants and computes pass/fail.
  - Console and API surfaces for preview, apply, monitor, and rollback.

- Data model (description):
  - RouteProfile: route_id, model_variant, median_length, p95_length, cold_start_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, tokens_per_minute (sampled), last_updated
  - Suggestion: id, bundle_params (batch_size; pad_to; cache_ttl_ms; quant_profile), est_cost_delta_pct, est_latency_delta_pct, confidence_score, rationale_ids
  - ExperimentRun: id, route_id, suggestion_id, start_time, percent_traffic, status, results_summary

- API endpoints (examples)
  - GET /v1/optimize/profiles?route={route_id}
  - POST /v1/optimize/suggestions/preview {route, suggestion_template} -> returns estimated deltas
  - POST /v1/optimize/experiments {suggestion_id, percent} -> schedules run
  - POST /v1/optimize/apply {suggestion_id, scope} -> apply globally or to route

- Console UX principles
  - Preview-first: always show estimated cost/latency/quality deltas and the profile driving the suggestion.
  - Safety-first: require eval pass or manual approval for high-risk changes (configurable by customer).
  - Visibility: expose per-token cost breakdown pre/post and a rollback CTA visible in the experiment card.

Roadmap & themes (quarterly view)
- Q2 2026 (MVP rollout): profiling + suggestion engine (R-001, R-002), console preview UI, experiment runner (canary), eval integration (R-004). Pilot with 5 customers.
- Q3 2026 (scale & automation): automated experiments with statistical tests and auto-rollback (R-003), one-click apply/rollback (R-005), initial billing integration for Optimize Pro (R-006).
- Q4 2026 (enterprise & private): advanced quantization profiles, VPC/private deployment integrations, reserved-capacity incentives and partner docs.

Pricing & packaging guidance
- Positioning: Redwood Optimize will be a monetized add-on with a free trial and three tiers:
  - Optimize Basic (free): profiling + up to 3 suggestion previews per month, community support.
  - Optimize Pro (paid): unlimited suggestions, automated experiments, billing credits for reserved capacity (e.g., 10-25% off inference unit price when paired with a 6-12 month Dedicated commitment).
  - Optimize Enterprise (custom): private deployment support, on-prem evals, account management, SLO-backed rollback SLAs.
- Billing rules (examples):
  - Suggestions and experiments billable as feature usage: Suggestions consumed per route per month (first 100 suggestions free in Pro).
  - Reserved capacity discounts applied via billing contract; Optimize Pro must be linked to a dedicated commit to qualify for max discount.
  - Audit logs and eval retention beyond 90 days are billable add-ons.

Release notes - v4.0 (initial pilot)
- New: workload profiler capturing p50/p95 lengths, cache hit rates, and cold-start metrics.
- New: suggestion engine returns ranked optimization bundles with estimated cost/latency deltas.
- New: UI preview for bundle suggestions with a simulated cost delta and rollout preview.
- New: experiment runner for canary A-B testing with automatic metric collection and rollback hooks.
- New: eval integration allowing pre/post runs on customer prompt sets for regression detection.
- Updated: documentation, API endpoints, and SDK examples for suggestion preview and experiment orchestration.

Rollout & launch plan
1) Internal alpha (2 weeks): ship profiler + suggestion engine to internal tenants; gather telemetry and iterate.
2) Private pilot (6-10 weeks): onboard 5 pilot customers (mix of startups + one enterprise). Track cost, latency, and quality metrics weekly.
3) Beta (8-12 weeks): wider opt-in (self-serve in console for Basic/Pro); telemetry guardrails and billing integration enabled.
4) GA (conditional on meeting success metrics): public documentation, pricing announced, and GTM materials for sales.

Operational requirements & runbooks
- Monitoring: dashboards for cost delta, P95 latency, experiment failure rate, and rollback frequency. Define alert thresholds: experiment failure rate >5% in 24h triggers review.
- Runbooks: step-by-step rollback, investigation checklist (signal sources: eval failures, increased client-side retries, model output drift), and escalation path to eng-sre and product.

Security & compliance notes
- Profiling telemetry will be sanitized to remove user PII and any customer payloads before storage.
- Eval prompt sets are stored encrypted; only authorized users can run/preview them.
- Feature classified as internal; any pilot customer material requiring confidentiality must be flagged and handled by security-and-compliance.

Open decisions / ADRs to create
- ADR-XXXX: thresholding policy for automated rollback vs. manual approval (risk/impact categories).
- ADR-XXXX: default quantization profiles we allow for auto-apply vs. those requiring manual opt-in.
